title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
layout_note: Overview panel is a grid: one column per item position, layers stacked upward, cross-position arrows showing attention direction; layer detail at left, baseline panels at right.
grouping: Four sub-figures in a row with italic sub-captions (a)-(d): (a) the Transformer layer in a dotted frame with a small 'Trm' tag, (b) the proposed model in the centre without a frame and largest, (c) and (d) two baseline models stacked at right, each in a dotted frame. An 'L×' with a curly brace at the left of (b) groups the repeated layers; a sideways 'Embedding Layer' label and brace group the embedding rows.
shapes_depth: Flat rectangles with thin dark outlines, no shadows, pastel fills: Trm blocks light green, item embeddings pink, position embeddings peach, Projection a brighter green; inside (a) Multi-Head Attention is light orange, Feed-Forward light blue, Dropout pale green and Add & Norm pale yellow, with residual lines looping round the side. Each sequence position is a column (v1 … vt-1 … [mask] at the bottom) with ellipses between columns. Thin black arrows connect every block in one layer to every block in the next (b), only to the same and later positions (c), or only to the next GRU in a horizontal chain (d).
proposed_highlight: The proposed model is the central, largest panel, the only one without a dotted frame, and the only one with a [mask] input token and a Projection head on top; the baselines are reduced, framed copies built from the same block shapes and colours.
lesson: Draw the proposed sequence model and its baselines with identical blocks (same green Trm boxes, same pink item cells v1 … vt) so that the only visible difference is the connection pattern between positions: all-to-all for bidirectional, forward-only for causal, a chain for recurrent.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page (CIKM '19). layout 'other': one column per sequence position with layers stacked bottom-to-top; baselines framed at right. elements 'other' = the all-to-all connection lines between layers.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: modality is a sequence of item IDs from user interaction histories; 'tabular' is the closest list item

insights.structure: Four captioned sub-figures in a row: (a) the Transformer layer in a dotted frame at far left, (b) the proposed model large and unframed in the centre, (c) SASRec and (d) the RNN baseline stacked in dotted frames at right, all drawn as one column per sequence position.
insights.data: Inputs are italic item symbols v1 ... v_{t-1} and a literal [mask] under each column, turned into pink item-embedding and peach position-embedding boxes joined by bold '+' signs; outputs are hidden states h^L and the predicted item v_t on top.
insights.emphasis: The proposed model is the biggest, the only one without a frame, and the only one with a [mask] token and a bright green Projection head, while baselines reuse the same green Trm/pink embedding blocks so the difference is only in the arrow pattern (all-to-all vs left-to-right vs GRU chain).
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside every panel; between layers the arrows encode the attention direction (every block to every block in b, only to same/later positions in c, horizontal chain in d), and an L× brace at the left of (b) groups the repeated layers.
insights.avoid: The all-to-all crossing arrows between Trm rows in (b) form a dense thicket of diagonals, and the sideways 'Embedding Layer' label is hard to read; do not copy the crossing-arrow mesh for more than three columns.

arrangement.units: four sub-figures captioned (a)-(d) below: (a), (c), (d) enclosed by dotted rectangles; (b) the proposed model unframed and widest; each panel holds a column-per-position stack of embedding and Trm/GRU boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: italic item ids v1 ... v_{t-1} and the literal [mask] token under each column, feeding pink+peach embedding boxes
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the predicted item v_t sits on top of the Projection box at the top of (b)
arrangement.shared: the Trm block is detailed once in (a) and reused as identical green 'Trm' boxes in (b) and (c); the same pink embedding boxes appear in all model panels
